overviewParagraphs: Thanh Lanh Valley Golf & Resort has earned the affectionate nickname "the Switzerland of Vietnam" — a title that captures the serene, alpine character of its stunning highland setting in Vinh Phuc Province. A massive natural lake sits at the heart of the resort, with towering forest-clad peaks rising on all sides and cool mountain breezes providing welcome relief from the Vietnamese heat.

The golf course works sympathetically with the natural landscape, using the lake as both a visual centrepiece and a strategic water feature on multiple holes. The routing balances short, risk-reward par fours with longer, more measured challenges, providing a thoroughly enjoyable experience for a wide range of handicaps.

Thanh Lanh Valley is one of the North's great weekend destinations for the visiting discerning golfer — close enough to Hanoi for a comfortable day trip, but immersive enough in its mountain and lakeside setting to feel entirely worlds away from the city.

curatorBriefHtml: Thanh Lanh Valley Golf & Resort (opened 2021 in Vinh Phuc Province) is Sir Nick Faldo’s alpine-styled Northern Vietnam masterpiece — nestled in a tranquil misty valley against the Tam Dao mountain range and bordering the serene waters of Thanh Lanh Lake. Measuring 6,793 yards from the Blue Tees (Par 72, stretching past 7,350 yards from the tips), the layout blends dramatic lakeside carries with rolling pine-framed fairways and a grand European-chateau clubhouse.

Having played Thanh Lanh Valley personally, it is easily one of the finest modern courses anywhere in Northern Vietnam. Conditioning is consistently crisp, the cool Tam Dao micro-climate keeps temperatures noticeably fresher than downtown Hanoi, and Faldo’s green complexes offer classic strategic angles without feeling unfair. Holes skirting Thanh Lanh Lake on the back nine deliver postcard views on every swing.

Situated just 60–70 minutes northwest of central Hanoi (and only 40 minutes from Noi Bai International Airport), Thanh Lanh Valley is a must-play headline round on The Emperor’s Fairways, pairing naturally with Sky Lake and BRG Kings Island.

scorecard.verdict: Often called the 'Switzerland of Vietnam,' Thanh Lanh Valley sits 1,000 meters above sea level beside a mirrored alpine lake. Cool breezes, dramatic elevation shifts, and a fairy-tale European clubhouse.

faqs.q: Why is Thanh Lanh Valley Golf & Resort called the 'Switzerland of Vietnam'?
faqs.a: Set beside crystal-clear Thanh Lanh Lake beneath the cool, misty peaks of the Tam Dao mountain range — anchored by a European chateau-style clubhouse — the setting feels dramatically cooler and more alpine than typical tropical courses.

faqs.q: How far is Thanh Lanh Valley from Hanoi and Noi Bai International Airport?
faqs.a: Thanh Lanh Valley sits roughly 40–45 minutes from Noi Bai International Airport (HAN) and 65–75 minutes northwest of central Hanoi via private touring vehicle.

faqs.q: What kind of test did Sir Nick Faldo design at Thanh Lanh Valley?
faqs.a: Faldo built an engaging, strategic Par 72 layout (6,793 yards Blue Tees) combining generous mountain-valley tee shots with clever lake-hugging risk-reward holes and undulating, well-bunkered greens.

faqs.q: When is the best time of year to play Thanh Lanh Valley?
faqs.a: October through April is prime dry season with crisp 16–25°C valley air; even during Hanoi’s warmer May–September months, Thanh Lanh’s Tam Dao foothills stay noticeably cooler.
